title: What knowledge and competence does MiFID II require of investment staff?
description: What MiFID II Article 25(1) and the ESMA guidelines require of staff who advise or give investment information: qualification, experience, annual review.
shortAnswer: Article 25(1) of the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive, Directive 2014/65/EU (MiFID II), requires investment firms to ensure, and demonstrate to regulators on request, that staff giving investment advice or information about financial instruments and services have the necessary knowledge and competence. European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) guidelines set the criteria: an appropriate qualification, at least six months of appropriate experience, an annual review, and supervision for staff not yet qualified.
keyTakeaways: Article 25(1) of MiFID II covers natural persons who give investment advice or information about financial instruments, investment services, or ancillary services on behalf of an investment firm, and Member States must publish the assessment criteria.
ESMA's Guidelines for the assessment of knowledge and competence (ESMA71-1154262120-153) have applied since January 3, 2018 and set a higher standard for advice than for giving information.
Staff need an appropriate qualification and appropriate experience of at least six months full-time equivalent; until then they may work only under supervision, for a maximum of four years.
Firms must review staff development and experience needs at least annually, keep staff current through continuous professional development, and train them before new products are offered.
Breaching Article 25(1) is a listed MiFID II infringement, with minimum maximum fines for legal persons of at least EUR 5,000,000 or up to 10% of annual turnover under Article 70(6).
regulator: National competent authorities designated under Article 67 of MiFID II, with the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) issuing guidelines
appliesTo: Investment firms and credit institutions providing investment services, including when selling or advising on structured deposits
UCITS management companies and external alternative investment fund managers providing individual portfolio management or non-core services
Staff, including tied agents, who give investment advice or information about financial instruments, structured deposits, investment services, or ancillary services to clients
Not staff who only point clients to information, hand over documents without comment, or perform back-office functions without client contact (ESMA examples)

sections.heading: What does MiFID II Article 25(1) require?

blocks.text: Article 25(1) puts the burden of proof on the firm. Staff who advise or inform clients must have the knowledge and competence their conduct duties require, and the firm must be able to show it.

blocks.title: Directive 2014/65/EU, Article 25(1)
blocks.text: "Member States shall require investment firms to ensure and demonstrate to competent authorities on request that natural persons giving investment advice or information about financial instruments, investment services or ancillary services to clients on behalf of the investment firm possess the necessary knowledge and competence to fulfil their obligations under Article 24 and this Article. Member States shall publish the criteria to be used for assessing such knowledge and competence."

Recital 79 explains why: because of the complexity of investment products and continuous innovation, staff who advise on or sell investment products to retail clients need an appropriate level of knowledge and competence, and firms "should allow their staff sufficient time and resources to achieve that knowledge and competence". Article 25(9) required ESMA to adopt guidelines specifying the assessment criteria.

Under Article 93 of the [current consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02014L0065-20260606), Member States have applied MiFID II since January 3, 2018. Article 25(1) reads the same in the consolidated version of June 6, 2026 as in the [original 2014 text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32014L0065). This page states the position as at November 2026.

sections.heading: What do the ESMA guidelines on knowledge and competence require?

blocks.text: The [ESMA Guidelines for the assessment of knowledge and competence](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/library/esma71-1154262120-153_guidelines_for_the_assessment_of_knowledge_and_competence_corrigendum.pdf) (ESMA71-1154262120-153 EN (rev), dated January 3, 2017) apply from January 3, 2018. Competent authorities and firms "must make every effort to comply" under Article 16(3) of the ESMA Regulation, and the guidelines set minimum standards that national authorities can raise.

blocks.caption: Core definitions and rules in the ESMA guidelines (as at November 2026)
head: Term or rule
ESMA guideline
Practical meaning
rows: An appropriate qualification plus appropriate experience to meet Articles 24 and 25 obligations
A qualification or other test or training course that meets the guidelines' criteria
Successfully demonstrated ability through previous work, for at least six months full-time equivalent; authorities may require longer
Staff lacking qualification or experience may serve clients only under a qualified, experienced supervisor, for no more than four years
Advice requires a higher standard; separate criteria lists for each
The compliance function assesses compliance with the guidelines and reports to the management body

blocks.text: For staff giving information, paragraph 17 lists ten areas, including key characteristics, risks, and features of products, total costs and charges, how financial markets work, the difference between past performance and future scenarios, market abuse and anti-money laundering, and reading documents such as Key Investor Information Documents and prospectuses. For advisers, paragraph 18 adds the ability to fulfill suitability obligations, to understand why a product may not be suitable for a client, and the fundamentals of managing a portfolio, including diversification.

sections.heading: How often must knowledge and competence be reviewed?

blocks.text: At least once a year. Paragraph 20(b) requires firms to "carry out an internal or external review, on at least an annual basis, of staff members' development and experience needs", to assess regulatory developments, and to act on them.

That review must also ensure staff keep their appropriate qualification and "maintain and update their knowledge and competence by undertaking continuous professional development or training", plus "specific training required in advance of any new investment products being offered by the firm". The guidelines do not set a number of continuing professional development hours; national authorities may. ESMA's illustrative examples describe ongoing assessment that uses updated material, tests knowledge of regulatory changes and new products, and includes verification questions, which can be delivered through courses, seminars, or independent study.

sections.heading: What records and supervision arrangements must a firm keep?

blocks.text: Firms must be able to give their competent authority, on request, records that let it "assess and verify compliance" with the guidelines (paragraph 20(c)). Those records are the practical answer to Article 25(1)'s duty to demonstrate.

items: **Role descriptions:** a clear distinction between giving advice and giving information, where relevant (paragraph 19).
**Qualification and experience:** evidence of the appropriate qualification and of experience in providing relevant services (paragraph 20(a)).
**Annual review:** the record of each year's review of development and experience needs and the actions taken (paragraph 20(b)).

**Supervision:** who supervises each unqualified staff member, how supervision is tailored, the supervisor's own competence, sign-off of suitability reports, and the start date so the four-year limit can be tracked (paragraphs 20(d) to (h)).

blocks.text: For assembling the file, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit). Tied agents are covered separately too: Article 29(3) allows them onto the public register only if they are of good repute and have "appropriate general, commercial and professional knowledge and competence".

sections.heading: What are the penalties for breaching Article 25(1)?

blocks.text: Article 70(3)(a)(xi) lists Article 25(1) to (6) among the provisions whose breach Member States must treat as an infringement. For those infringements, Article 70(6) requires national authorities to have at least the powers to issue public statements, cease and desist orders, management bans, and suspension or withdrawal of authorization.

The minimum maximum fines are at least EUR 5,000,000 or up to 10% of total annual turnover for legal persons, at least EUR 5,000,000 for natural persons, and at least twice the benefit derived where it can be determined. National law sets the actual penalties within those floors.

sections.heading: How do national rules, including Portugal's, apply the requirement?

blocks.text: Because MiFID II is a directive and Article 25(1) asks each Member State to publish its own criteria, firms must follow national qualification lists or criteria as well as the ESMA guidelines. Paragraphs 21 to 23 of the guidelines require competent authorities to publish either a list of appropriate qualifications or the criteria they must meet, plus the required experience period, the maximum supervision period, and whether qualification reviews are done by the firm or an external body.

Portugal transposed MiFID II mainly through Lei n.º 35/2018 of July 20, which amended the rules on marketing financial products and on the organization of financial intermediaries, according to the [EUR-Lex national transposition record](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/NIM/?uri=CELEX:32014L0065). Firms in Portugal should take the published qualification and experience criteria from their competent authority, such as the Comissão do Mercado de Valores Mobiliários (CMVM), rather than from this summary. The insurance equivalent is covered in [IDD CPD requirements](/regulations/insurance-distribution-directive-cpd-requirements).

blocks.text: A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) that separates advice roles from information roles makes the annual review straightforward. For assessment design, see [how to design competency assessments](/guides/how-to-design-competency-assessments).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the ESMA criteria, products, and client-facing roles as linked concepts with assessment points, so each role's required knowledge is explicit and testable. When a new product or rule arrives, the affected roles and assessments are identified from those links, supporting the annual review and pre-launch training. See [financial services](/industries/financial-services).

faqs.q: How many CPD hours does MiFID II require each year?
faqs.a: MiFID II and the ESMA guidelines set no fixed number of hours. The guidelines require at least an annual review of each staff member's development and experience needs and continuous professional development or training to maintain the appropriate qualification. Some national competent authorities set hours, so check the home Member State's published criteria.

faqs.q: Can new staff advise clients before they are qualified?
faqs.a: Only under supervision. Staff without an appropriate qualification or appropriate experience may provide relevant services only under a supervisor who has both, who takes responsibility as if providing the service, and who signs off suitability reports. The maximum period under supervision is four years, or shorter if the authority requires.

faqs.q: Do call center staff who only send documents fall under MiFID II knowledge and competence?
faqs.a: Usually not. ESMA's examples place outside scope employees who only point clients to information, distribute brochures, or hand over documents such as a Key Investor Information Document without commenting on content, and back-office staff without client contact. Once staff explain products or services, they are in scope.

faqs.q: Who checks compliance with the ESMA knowledge and competence guidelines inside a firm?
faqs.a: The compliance function. Paragraph 16 of the guidelines says it should assess and review compliance with the guidelines and include that review in its report to the management body on the implementation and effectiveness of the control environment for investment services.
